raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Part of #43147, for the GLM-4.7 / GLM-5 parser.

#43147 reports that `parse_arguments` in `glm4_moe_detector.py` falls back to `ast.literal_eval`, which turns a bare comma into a Python tuple, so a scalar the model wrote as `1,000` reaches the tool as the JSON array `[1, 0]`. #43264 fixes that file.

`glm47_moe_detector.py` (used by `--tool-call-parser glm47` for GLM-4.7 and GLM-5) has its own copy of `parse_arguments` with the same Strategy 3 and the same bug, and #43264 doesn't touch it. On current main:

```
parse_arguments("1,000", "number")   -> ((1, 0), True)
Glm47MoeDetector, <arg_value>1,000</arg_value> for a number param -> {"n": [1, 0]}   (streaming and non-streaming)
```

## Modifications

- `glm47_moe_detector.py`: when Strategy 3 returns a tuple, fall through to Strategy 4 (keep the raw string), unless the argument is array-typed. Array-typed arguments get the tuple as a list, which is exactly what the client saw before (`json.dumps` already turned the tuple into an array), so `1, 2` for an array param still becomes `[1, 2]`. Only non-array arguments change.
- `test_glm47_schema_types.py`:
  - `test_bare_comma_value_is_not_split_into_an_array` runs end to end through `Glm47MoeDetector` with the existing `check_arguments` helper (non-streaming, plus streaming at chunk sizes 1, 7 and full).
  - `test_parse_arguments_bare_comma` covers the reported inputs and pins the array-typed behaviour.

Both tests fail on current main and pass with this change. Tests live in the GLM-4.7 test file, so this doesn't overlap with #43264's changes.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A: parser-only change, no change to model forward or kernels.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A.

## Tests run

CPU-only (Python 3.13, torch 2.14.1+cpu, Linux container):

```
python -m pytest test/registered/unit/function_call/
631 passed, 1633 subtests passed
```

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests (bug regression; fails on main, passes with the fix).
- [ ] Update documentation (N/A).
- [ ] Accuracy/speed benchmarks (N/A, parser-only).

detail.title: [Fix] GLM-4.7/5 tool parser: stop turning comma-containing values into arrays

files.patch:
@@ -286,7 +286,12 @@ def parse_arguments(
     # Strategy 3: ast.literal_eval
     try:
         parsed_value = safe_literal_eval(json_value)
-        return parsed_value, True
+        # A bare comma makes literal_eval build a tuple ("1,000" -> (1, 0));
+        # only an array-typed argument may take it, as a list.
+        if not isinstance(parsed_value, tuple):
+            return parsed_value, True
+        if arg_type == "array":
+            return list(parsed_value), True
     except (ValueError, SyntaxError):
         pass

@@ -2,7 +2,10 @@
 import unittest
 
 from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Function, Tool
-from sglang.srt.function_call.glm47_moe_detector import Glm47MoeDetector
+from sglang.srt.function_call.glm47_moe_detector import (
+    Glm47MoeDetector,
+    parse_arguments,
+)
 from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
 
 register_cpu_ci(est_time=2, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
@@ -357,6 +360,20 @@ def test_completed_arguments_reset_between_tool_calls(self):
             {"value": "hello"},
         )
 
+    def test_bare_comma_value_is_not_split_into_an_array(self):
+        """#43147: "1,000" for a number arg reached the tool as [1, 0]."""
+        self.check_arguments(
+            {"type": "object", "properties": {"n": {"type": "number"}}},
+            {"n": "1,000"},
+        )
+
+    def test_parse_arguments_bare_comma(self):
+        """#43147: literal_eval turns a bare comma into a tuple. Non-array args
+        keep the raw string; array args keep the list they got before."""
+        self.assertEqual(parse_arguments("1,000", "number"), ("1,000", True))
+        self.assertEqual(parse_arguments('"a","b"', "object"), ('"a","b"', True))
+        self.assertEqual(parse_arguments("1, 2", "array"), ([1, 2], True))
+
 
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()
